result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A keeps the old results and pins visible for the whole wait. It also says when a skeleton would be appropriate (panning to a new city) and reserves space for the error banner. B handles the map better, with faded pins and an 'Updating homes…' pill, and covers more failure cases (first load, partial failure). But after 1 s, B replaces the list with skeletons, which breaks its own rule of keeping the old results visible. A's weak point is that it deliberately shows nothing on the map while loading. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B is the more internally consistent design. It keeps old results dimmed for the whole wait, explains when a skeleton is and isn't appropriate, and reserves space so the error banner doesn't shift the list. A puts indicators in more places, including the map, but its 1s+ skeletons replace the stale results, which contradicts its own rule of keeping them visible. B's single-indicator approach leaves the map without any local loading cue.
